the role of phospholipase enzymes in the diabetic heart and their potential as therapeutic targets for heart disease in diabetes.

the identification of the mechanisms by which phospholipases contribute to the development of diabetic cardiomyopathy, and how these mechanisms could be used as therapeutic targets for the prevention and treatment of heart failure in diabetes.

there is no conclusive evidence for any specific phospholipase to be responsible for the development of diabetic cardiomyopathy.
phospholipid metabolism is an important component of diabetic cardiomyopathy.

the phospholipases A2, C, and D, and their downstream signaling mechanisms play important roles in the pathophysiology and treatment of diabetic cardiomyopathy.

the defects in phosphoinositide and diacylglycerol signal transduction, and the resultant changes in the levels and/or activities of various phospholipid-dependent enzymes, are likely to be important in the pathophysiology and progression of diabetic cardiomyopathy.

the heart is highly susceptible to phospholipid abnormalities in diabetes, which are mediated by the activation of different phospholipes, including phospholipase D, A2 and C. These
